questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Animals whose cells are arranged as loose cell aggregates, showing the cellular level of organisation, belong to:

solution.explanation: Sponges (Porifera) show the cellular level: their cells form loose aggregates and do not form true tissues. Coelenterates show the tissue level, and Platyhelminthes and higher groups show organ and organ-system levels.
steps: Organ / organ-system level → Platyhelminthes, annelids and higher phyla
solution.why_others_wrong: Coelenterates already have tissues; flatworms and annelids have organs and organ systems.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Animal Kingdom', basis of classification: levels of organisation
solution.final_answer: Option A: Porifera

questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In cartilaginous fishes, the teeth are modified placoid scales which are backwardly directed.
Statement II: In cartilaginous fishes, the gill slits are covered by an operculum.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

solution.explanation: Chondrichthyes have placoid scales, and their teeth are modified placoid scales pointing backwards: Statement I is true. Their gill slits are separate and without an operculum (gill cover); the operculum is a feature of bony fishes (Osteichthyes): Statement II is false.

Gill slits separate, no operculum in Chondrichthyes → II false

solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.question_text:

Statement I: In Urochordata, the notochord is present only in the larval tail.
Statement II: In Cephalochordata, the notochord extends from head to tail and persists throughout life.

Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Protochordates: position and persistence of the notochord

steps: Urochordata → notochord only in larval tail → I true
Cephalochordata → head to tail, throughout life → II true

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Cyclostomes have a sucking and circular mouth without jaws.
Statement II: Cyclostomes are freshwater animals that migrate to the sea for spawning.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Cyclostomes (Petromyzon, Myxine) have a jawless, sucking, circular mouth: Statement I is true. They are marine but migrate to fresh water for spawning; they die after spawning, and the larvae return to the ocean after metamorphosis. Statement II reverses the direction, so it is false.
steps: Jawless circular sucking mouth → I true
Marine animals that spawn in fresh water → II false
solution.why_others_wrong: Students who remember 'migration for spawning' but not its direction mark both true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Animal Kingdom', Class Cyclostomata
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Hemichordata is now placed as a separate phylum under non-chordates.
Reason (R): Hemichordates have an open circulatory system, and their excretory organ is the proboscis gland.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Hemichordata was earlier treated as a sub-phylum of Chordata and is now a separate phylum under non-chordates: A is true. Their circulation is open and the proboscis gland is the excretory organ: R is true. But these are general features of the phylum and say nothing about why it was moved out of Chordata.
steps: A: earlier a chordate sub-phylum, now a non-chordate phylum → true
R: open circulatory system, proboscis gland for excretion → true
R does not address the classification change → R does not explain A
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A is the trap: both statements are true, but R describes the animals, not their placement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Animal Kingdom', Phylum Hemichordata
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

solution.concept: Skin and body-covering features of chordate classes

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Simple squamous epithelium, made of a single thin layer of flattened cells, is found in:

Cuboidal → ducts of glands, tubular parts of nephrons

steps: Goblet cell = single secretory cell → unicellular gland
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', animal tissues: glandular epithelium

questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Compound epithelium has a limited role in secretion and absorption.
Reason (R): Compound epithelium is made of more than one layer of cells.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

solution.concept: Structure decides function in compound epithelium
solution.explanation: Because compound epithelium is multi-layered, substances cannot easily pass across it, so it has only a limited role in secretion and absorption. Its main function is protection against chemical and mechanical stresses. R is the reason for A.
steps: Multi-layered → poor secretion/absorption → A true and explained by R

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the frog are correct?

(a) Frogs never drink water but absorb it through the skin.
(b) A frog has a distinct neck and a short tail.
(c) The forelimbs end in four digits and the hind limbs end in five digits.
(d) In water, the skin acts as an aquatic respiratory organ.
(e) The frog is a warm-blooded animal.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The frog absorbs water through its skin and uses the skin for respiration in water (cutaneous respiration). Its forelimbs end in four digits and the larger hind limbs in five. Its body is divided into head and trunk only, and it is cold-blooded (poikilotherm).
steps: (b) False: neck and tail are absent

questions.subject: Zoology

solution.explanation: NCERT classifies connective tissue as loose, dense and specialised. Loose connective tissue includes areolar tissue and adipose tissue. Adipose cells store fats; excess nutrients are converted into fat and stored here.
steps: Loose connective tissue → areolar and adipose
Dense regular → tendons, ligaments; dense irregular → skin
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', animal tissues: loose connective tissue

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about muscle tissue are correct?

(a) Smooth muscle fibres taper at both ends and do not show striations.
(b) Cardiac muscle cells have communication junctions (intercalated discs) that allow the cells to contract as a unit.
(c) Skeletal muscle fibres are involuntary.
(d) Smooth muscle is found in the walls of blood vessels, stomach and intestine.
(e) Cardiac muscle tissue is found in the heart and in the walls of large arteries.

solution.explanation: Smooth muscle fibres are fusiform and unstriated, and line the walls of internal organs such as blood vessels, stomach and intestine. questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In female frogs, the ureters act as urinogenital ducts.
Reason (R): In male frogs, the vasa efferentia from the testes enter the kidneys and communicate with the urinogenital duct that opens into the cloaca.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In male frogs, the ureters carry both urine and sperms (urinogenital ducts), because the 10–12 vasa efferentia from the testes enter the kidneys and reach the urinogenital duct. In female frogs, the ureters and oviducts open separately into the cloaca. So A is false and R is true.
steps: Female frog: ureters and oviducts separate → A false
Male frog: vasa efferentia → kidney → urinogenital duct → cloaca → R true
solution.why_others_wrong: A applies the male arrangement to the female, which is the trap.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', frog: anatomy, excretory and reproductive systems
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Tight junctions help to stop substances from leaking across a tissue.
Statement II: Gap junctions perform cementing to keep neighbouring cells together.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Tight junctions stop substances from leaking across a tissue: Statement I is true. Cementing that keeps neighbouring cells together is done by adhering junctions; gap junctions connect the cytoplasm of adjoining cells for rapid transfer of ions, small molecules and sometimes big molecules: Statement II is false.
steps: Adhering → cementing; gap → cytoplasmic communication (II false)
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II gives the gap junction the function of the adhering junction.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', animal tissues: cell junctions
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

options.text: Its RBCs are nucleated and contain haemoglobin.

questions.subject: Zoology

On grinding, cell membranes break into pieces and form vesicles that are not water-soluble

Trichloroacetic acid converts them into proteins

questions.subject: Zoology

solution.explanation: In an amino acid, the α-carbon carries four substituents: hydrogen, a carboxyl group, an amino group and a variable R group, so amino acids are substituted methanes: Statement I is true. Glycine: R = H; alanine: R = CH₃; serine: R = hydroxymethyl (II false)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Malonate inhibits the enzyme succinic dehydrogenase because malonate:

Raises the activation energy of the uncatalysed reaction

solution.explanation: Prosthetic groups (such as haem) are tightly bound to the apoenzyme. Co-enzymes are bound only transiently, usually during catalysis, and many contain vitamins. questions.subject: Zoology

External inter-costals contract during inspiration → R false

Have no effect, because the heart is myogenic

questions.subject: Zoology

Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

Atrial systole adds about 30% of ventricular filling, not 70% → II false
solution.why_others_wrong: NCERT gives about 30 per cent for the increase due to atrial systole; Statement II inflates it, so options A and B fail.

Vasodilation and a fall in blood pressure

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the mechanism of muscle contraction are correct?

(a) Acetylcholine released at the neuromuscular junction generates an action potential in the sarcolemma.
(b) The action potential spreads through the muscle fibre and causes the release of Ca²⁺ into the sarcoplasm.
(c) The myosin head binds to the exposed active sites on actin to form a cross bridge.
(d) During relaxation, Ca²⁺ is pumped back into the sarcoplasmic cisternae.
(e) The Ca²⁺ that triggers contraction is released from the mitochondria of the muscle fibre.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: A neural signal releases acetylcholine at the motor end plate, generating an action potential in the sarcolemma. Ca²⁺ is released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum, the store of calcium ions, and binds troponin, exposing the active sites on actin for myosin heads. Cross bridges form and pull actin. During relaxation Ca²⁺ is pumped back into the sarcoplasmic cisternae.
steps: (e) False: the Ca²⁺ comes from the sarcoplasmic reticulum, not mitochondria
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', mechanism of muscle contraction
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

Statement II: The 11th and 12th pairs of ribs are called vertebrochondral (false) ribs.

Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The first seven pairs join the sternum ventrally through hyaline cartilage: true ribs. So Statement I is true and Statement II is false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', skeletal system: rib cage
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

It is formed by 26 serially arranged units called vertebrae

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about contractile proteins are correct?

(a) Each actin (thin) filament is made of two F-actins helically wound to each other.
(b) Each F-actin is a polymer of monomeric G-actins.
(c) In the resting state, a subunit of troponin masks the active binding sites for myosin on the actin filaments.
(d) Each myosin (thick) filament is a polymer of monomeric proteins called meromyosins.
(e) The tail of the meromyosin, the light meromyosin (LMM), has ATPase activity.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Thin filaments are two helically wound F-actins (polymers of G-actin) with tropomyosin running along them and troponin at intervals. Thick filaments are polymers of meromyosin. Each meromyosin has a globular head with a short arm (heavy meromyosin, HMM) and a tail (light meromyosin, LMM). The globular head is the active ATPase and has binding sites for ATP and actin.
steps: (e) False: ATPase activity is in the globular head (HMM part)
solution.why_others_wrong: (e) moves the ATPase from the head to the tail; the head is what binds actin and ATP.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', structure of contractile proteins
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In each cycle, the sodium-potassium pump transports 3 Na⁺ out of the axon and 2 K⁺ into it. After 150 cycles, the net number of positive charges moved from inside to outside the axon is:

solution.concept: Electrogenic nature of the Na⁺–K⁺ pump
solution.explanation: Each cycle moves 3 positive charges out and 2 in, a net outward movement of one positive charge. This helps make the outer surface of the resting membrane positive and the inner surface negative.
steps: Net per cycle = 3 − 2 = 1 positive charge outward
solution.why_others_wrong: 450 counts only the Na⁺ moved out; 300 counts only the K⁺ moved in; 750 adds both instead of taking the difference.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', generation and conduction of nerve impulse

Reason (R): The resting axonal membrane is more permeable to Na⁺ than to K⁺.

Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

solution.explanation: The resting membrane is polarised: inside negative, outside positive. A is true. The resting axonal membrane is comparatively more permeable to K⁺ and nearly impermeable to Na⁺, and the Na⁺–K⁺ pump maintains the ionic gradients. R reverses the permeabilities, so R is false.

Resting membrane: more permeable to K⁺, not Na⁺ → R false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', generation and conduction of nerve impulse
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: When a stimulus is applied at a site on a polarised axonal membrane, which sequence of events is correct?

options.text: Rise in permeability to K⁺ → K⁺ diffuses out → inside becomes positive → Na⁺ influx restores the resting potential
Membrane becomes freely permeable to Na⁺ → rapid efflux of Na⁺ → inside becomes more negative → K⁺ moves in
K⁺ rushes into the axon → inside becomes positive → Na⁺ diffuses out → resting potential restored
Membrane becomes freely permeable to Na⁺ → rapid influx of Na⁺ → reversal of polarity (inside positive) → rise in permeability to K⁺ → K⁺ diffuses out and the resting potential is restored

solution.explanation: At the stimulated site the membrane becomes freely permeable to Na⁺, leading to a rapid influx of Na⁺ and a reversal of polarity: the outer surface becomes negative and the inner surface positive (depolarised). This rise in Na⁺ permeability is short-lived and is quickly followed by a rise in permeability to K⁺. K⁺ diffuses out and restores the resting potential.
steps: K⁺ permeability rises → K⁺ efflux → resting potential restored
solution.why_others_wrong: The other sequences reverse the direction of Na⁺ or K⁺ movement or put K⁺ first.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', generation and conduction of nerve impulse
solution.final_answer: Option D: Membrane becomes freely permeable to Na⁺ → rapid influx of Na⁺ → reversal of polarity (inside positive) → rise in permeability to K⁺ → K⁺ diffuses out and the resting potential is restored
